title: Re-adjudicate the H22 compat ledger against LOCAL references
status_note: Every oracle item is met. Green does not mean the residual is small - 671 of H5's 1,267 remain UNVERIFIABLE and that is reported as the finding, not softened. Four of the leg's own instrument defects were caught by its own controls before emission and are recorded in findings (H7-F12).
settings_profile: harness/readonly-settings.json (READ-ONLY leg per R61; harness/notes/** is the only writable path). No pytest was run and no suite evidence is claimed - the leg touches no product code.
agents_note: No subagents dispatched. This leg is one deterministic data-analysis job whose every number must trace to a single producer script (Law 2); fanning it out would have split the producer path. The adversarial pass was run in-line as 25 named controls, each stating its own failure condition (Law 1), plus line-by-line inspection of every cell before emission.

read_only_discipline.no_repairs: Every defect found is a finding. Nothing was fixed, including the two doc-drift items and the census kind defect, all of which live outside harness/notes/**.
read_only_discipline.no_network: Zero fetches. Every oracle shipped inside Houdini 22.0.368 or is a prior leg's artifact. A network call would have reintroduced the version ambiguity R72 removed.

summary.h5_input: 1,267 UNVERIFIABLE of 3,115 symbols. Ledger sha256[:16] 0c8ad1d37266c8f7, leg H5, commit 0a88f5fbd840, model claude-opus-5[1m] - all four asserted by control C12. Read from the h5-compat worktree, not assumed merged.
summary.the_honest_headline: 47% of H5's largest bucket resolved (596 of 1,267). The brief expected reachability to be the dominant cause; it is not. Indexing the local oracles that existed and were never read - tops.zip, the build's shipped python source, and nodes.zip applied to the unprobed node rows - accounts for the 596. The remaining 671 is dominated by a CENSUS defect: 528 rows are bare method names with no dotted owner, 335 of them OpenUSD names recorded as hom_method. No documentation source can fix an unbound leaf.

findings.claim: This leg's own instrument was wrong four times and its own controls caught all four before emission. (1) A page-wide /deprecat/i detector reported 85 doc-side deprecations; most were deprecated PARAMETERS, MENU OPTIONS, LOCAL VARIABLES, and one member literally NAMED `deprecated`. The worst near-miss was flagging the LOP Reference node - 78 SYNAPSE occurrences - from `(`$IIDX` is deprecated)` at lop/reference.txt:58. (2) The prose marker still had no SUBJECT test, so 'this OPTION is deprecated' (dop/flipsolver.txt:146) and 'this WORKFLOW has been deprecated' (vop/kma_nesteddielectrics.txt:13) read as node deprecations - while five real ones ('This node is deprecated', sop/polyknit.txt:12 and four others) depend on that marker and would have been LOST by removing it. (3) The first adjudication re-derived existence instead of applying H5's SCOPE_LIMIT, so it called five real `hou.<module>.<member>` rows 'no Houdini referent' - the same defect H5's own CORRECTION records, pointed the other way - and classified the FILENAME `hdefereval.py` as a PHANTOM API. (4) The residual-shape characterisation tie-broke on set iteration order and reported 335/112/81 on one run and 338/110/80 on the next; it is now deterministic at 334/109/85 across three PYTHONHASHSEED values. After all four fixes the doc-side count is 39.
findings.anchor: controls C15, C16, C19, C23 (detector), C21, C22 (scope limit and filename), C24 (determinism), all in harness/notes/h7_controls.json
findings.severity: method finding, and the same shape as R60 and R71 - the reader every verdict depends on needed its own two-sided control. A single-sided detector would have shipped 46 false deprecations, one false phantom, five real symbols dismissed as non-Houdini, and a characterisation number that changes between runs. Every one of those was a confident, plausible result.

headline_findings: R72's doc_silent_deprecation cell holds at 2 members - karma and karmarenderproperties - now confirmed against the AUTHORITATIVE build-shipped node reference rather than a mutable browsing cache (H7-F2).

The DECAY_CLOCK floor moves 19 -> 41. The correction is almost entirely doc-side, and 17 of the 19 H5-vs-H7 disagreements trace to one unfollowed `:include` banner that hid the whole deprecated old-COPs surface (H7-F3, H7-F4).
Reachability was NOT the dominant cause of H5's 1,267. 596 resolved; of the 671 that remain, 528 are a census kind defect that no documentation source can fix (H7-F7).
method_notes: R60 applied literally: the reader was demonstrated against RopNode and TopNode BEFORE adjudicating anything, and the run aborts if any control fails. It did abort once - C10 failed on R72's cache character count, which turned out to be a finding about a cited number rather than a defect in the reader (H7-F6). The control was re-specified to test the reader, and the discrepancy was recorded instead of being absorbed.

R72's method note held for a third time: each of this leg's first results was plausible and wrong. Page-wide deprecation detection, re-derived existence, and a raw read of `deprecated_runtime` each produced a confident number that inspection destroyed.

H5's judgments were honoured, not silently overturned. Its category-scope resolutions (`duplicate` deprecated as a Sop, current as the Lop SYNAPSE calls; `cop2net` deprecated only as a Chop) are VERIFIED-RUNTIME findings that H7 has no evidence to outrank. C20 is two-sided on exactly this: it must drop those two AND keep karma, where H5 recorded `emission_category_resolved: Lop`.
Every residual now carries a NAMED reason. 'UNVERIFIABLE' with no reason is what made H5's 1,267 unreadable; the same total split six ways is actionable.

resume_token.redo_if: the Houdini build changes - every oracle here is pinned to 22.0.368 by construction, so a new major invalidates all of it at once. Also redo if the census is fixed to emit dotted owners, which is the change that would collapse the 528-row residual.
resume_token.do_not_attempt_again: resolving the leaf_unbound_owner bucket from documentation. It is not a documentation question. The owner is missing at the call site, and only the census can supply it.

for_ruling.question: Which corpus governs `pxr`? 79 rows are OUT_OF_REFERENCE_SCOPE:third_party - EXISTS is decided by the dir() table, but the H22 reference is not the deprecation authority for OpenUSD and no local OpenUSD reference is pinned. Calling them PRIVATE_API is a false alarm; leaving them UNVERIFIABLE implies a local oracle exists and was not read.
for_ruling.recommendation: Accept 'exists + third-party corpus' as a TERMINAL cell for pxr rather than a residual, and pin the OpenUSD version separately if pxr deprecation ever needs to be tracked. Do not let 79 rows sit in a bucket labelled 'unknown' when the only unknown is which vendor's release notes to read.

for_ruling.question: The 528-row leaf_unbound_owner bucket is a census defect: bare method names with no dotted owner, 335 of them OpenUSD. Fixing it means changing the census emitter, which lives under scripts/ and is outside a read-only leg's fence.
for_ruling.recommendation: Schedule the census fix as the next compat leg's FIRST item. It is the highest-yield change available - it would collapse 78% of the residual and correct the `kind` field so pxr names stop being adjudicated against the HOM reference.

for_ruling.question: 12 doc_only DECAY_CLOCK rows are bare leaves bound by owner-invariance - xRes, yRes, depth, saveImage, allPixels, setPixelsOfCookingPlane, Cop2Node, dirtyAllTasks, dirtyTasks, executeGraph, generateStaticItems, setUpdateMode. Every documented owner of each is deprecated, so the verdict does not depend on which owner the census meant - but that does not prove the call site is a HOM object at all.
for_ruling.recommendation: Promote to DECAY_CLOCK only after a code read binds the call sites. Until then they are leads. I have deliberately reported the floor as 41 WITH this caveat attached rather than quoting either bound alone: 29 is the owner-explicit total (2 doc_silent + 27 owner-explicit doc_only) and 41 includes the 12 conditional rows. Both are in the ledger; neither is quoted without the other.

for_ruling.question: `cop2net` (60 occurrences): the authored help deprecates manager/cop2net.txt via the old-COPs banner, while H5's runtime category resolution says SYNAPSE's sites are Lop/Driver where deprecationInfo() is silent and only Chop/cop2net is flagged. Same name, two sources, opposite answers - and R72 rule 3 says disagreement is itself a finding.
for_ruling.recommendation: Treat as a genuine two-source disagreement, not a resolved OK. The COP2 subsystem is vendor-deprecated in favour of Copernicus; a SYNAPSE surface still naming cop2net is a decay risk regardless of which category the runtime flags. Needs a code read to bind the 60 sites.

for_ruling.question: R72 cites two help-cache character counts that reproduce under no measure (H7-F6). The ruling's conclusion is confirmed; the numbers are not.
for_ruling.recommendation: Withdraw the two character counts from citation and replace them with the nodes.zip anchors, which are exact and offline-verifiable: lop/karmarenderproperties.txt 56,325 chars #since 18.0, lop/karma.txt 2,556 chars. Amending a ruling is a human act, so this is a ruling item and not a doc fix I would make.

for_ruling.question: 104 node_type rows are absent from the shipped node reference and were never probed live; 172 more are documented-and-current with EXISTS resting on the documented basis rather than a probe. A live node-type existence sweep would decide the first group and confirm the second.
for_ruling.recommendation: Schedule it, but not inside a read-only leg and not while a live session holds the licence. The brief scoped H7 to local references and H5's existing runtime verdicts, and I did not run hython for that reason - the absence of a probe is recorded on every affected row via exists_basis, never disguised as one.

for_ruling.question: `docs/sprint_freeze/marshal_map.md:527` cites `hdefereval.executeInMainThreadWithResultAndDelay`, which is not defined anywhere in the build's shipped source. A governing note names a nonexistent API.
for_ruling.recommendation: One-line doc fix, outside this leg's fence. Low severity - the code is already remediated and lint-guarded (H7-F9) - but it is exactly the shape Law 5 warns about: a claim sourced from recall of a prior design rather than from the tree.

for_ruling.question: Should the new deprecation-marker vocabulary and its two-sided controls be promoted out of harness/notes/ into a reusable checker? It is currently a producer script for one leg, and every future build will need the same five markers and the same four false-positive guards.
for_ruling.recommendation: Promote after the census fix (H7-R2), not before - the checker's input contract should be the corrected census, not the current one. Promotion means writing under scripts/, which no read-only leg can do.

what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis.the_brief_said: H5's UNVERIFIABLE:1267 is partly a REACHABILITY artifact, and the residual after fixing reachability is the real unknown.
what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis.the_leg_found: Half right, and the half that is wrong matters more. Reachability - in the broader sense of 'local oracles that existed and were never indexed' - accounts for the 595 resolutions. But the robots.txt framing was not the mechanism: hom.zip and nodes.zip were ALREADY H5's declared authority, named in its own docs_authority.paths. What was missing was tops.zip, the build's shipped python source, and the APPLICATION of nodes.zip to the 298 node rows H5's live probe never reached. And the true residual is dominated by something no reference could ever fix - 528 bare method names the census never bound to an owner.
what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis.the_correction_to_R72: R72's source table lists only the userprefs cache for the node axis and states that hom.zip 'cannot adjudicate karmarenderproperties at all'. Both are true of hom.zip. But the build ships nodes.zip beside it, H5 already cited it, and it settles the node axis authoritatively - which is why R72's headline finding could be re-tested on it and confirmed rather than merely re-asserted.
what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis.what_would_have_gone_wrong_without_contr: 46 false deprecations (including the LOP Reference node, 78 occurrences), one false phantom on a filename, five real hou.* members dismissed as 'not Houdini symbols', a third doc_silent_deprecation member (`duplicate`) that H5 had already proven was a category-scoped false alarm, and a residual characterisation that changed between runs. Every one of those was a confident, plausible number.
what_the_leg_proves_about_its_own_premis.the_ledger_is_1457648_bytes_and_reconcil: counts.arithmetic_check asserts 596 + 671 == 1267 inside the artifact, so a future edit that breaks the split fails loudly rather than reading as a new finding.
